live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a Rust ransomware-for-hire gang, from 2021 leak-site claims to a 2024 apparent exit scam
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, rented out Rust-built ransomware from late 2021. It listed victims from cities to insurers on a leak site, drew an FBI disruption in December 2023, then appeared to vanish in March 2024.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also tracked as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
Malpedia describes it as a Rust ransomware family sold as ransomware-as-a-service. It says the ransomware has been seen in attacks since 18 November 2021.
BleepingComputer reports that ALPHV is believed to be a rebrand of the DarkSide and BlackMatter ransomware operations.
S2W found that several BlackCat configuration fields match BlackMatter's exactly. It still found it difficult to conclude that the two are the same group.

BleepingComputer reports that the FBI linked the gang to over 60 breaches between November 2021 and March 2022. It also reports an FBI estimate of at least $300 million in ransoms from more than 1,000 victims, up to September 2023.
Recorded Future News says Black Cat/AlphV has made a point of going after healthcare and pharmaceutical companies.
A January 2023 news report says the gang listed the city of Alexandria, Louisiana, as a victim. The same report says the group had attacked at least three US colleges and universities that year.
Other reported victims include a Canadian software group, Constellation Software, and the dental and medical distributor Henry Schein.

BleepingComputer reports that the gang claimed the mortgage lender loanDepot and the insurer Prudential Financial on its leak site. The claims were unverified at the time, because the gang had not yet published proof.
Malpedia says the ransomware can be set to encrypt files with AES or ChaCha20. It can delete volume shadow copies, stop services and stop virtual machines on ESXi servers.
Malpedia also says it can spread across a local network by running itself on other hosts with PsExec.
Symantec describes updates in mid-2022. They added an ARM build and encryption through safe mode, and indexing of stolen data on the leak sites.
Symantec also saw an updated Exmatter data-theft tool used alongside the ransomware. It saw an affiliate use the Eamfo infostealer to target Veeam backup credentials.

Sygnia investigated a 2023 intrusion that it attributes to BlackCat or one of its affiliates. Access came through a third-party vendor's network. The attacker used Cobalt Strike for lateral movement and Rclone to copy data out, then sent extortion emails over roughly 45 days.
The group runs a leak site and threatens to publish stolen data. In a Hampton-Newport News CSB case, DataBreaches.Net reports a claim of over 800 GB and a 48-hour deadline.
CrowdStrike Intelligence assessed that affiliates were likely beginning to move toward ALPHV and AvosLocker ransomware-as-a-service programs.

In September 2022 the gang claimed an attack on Suffolk County, whose attack disabled the 911 system. It posted screenshots of the county's backup systems and claimed 400 GB of data. DataBreaches could not confirm the leak.
Cybernews reports that the gang listed the IT contractor NJVC on 28 September 2022, then removed the listing. The breach was the gang's own claim, and NJVC did not reply to a request for comment.
In May 2023 Constellation Software confirmed a breach of some internal systems. ALPHV claimed on its leak site to have stolen more than 1 TB.

In a statement on the MGM Resorts attack in September 2023, AlphV said it launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors on 11 September. These are AlphV's own claims, and the article does not verify them.
Henry Schein disclosed a cyber incident on 15 October. A report says AlphV (BlackCat) claimed responsibility and re-encrypted systems after negotiations broke down.
In December 2023 the FBI disrupted the gang's operation and temporarily took down its Tor negotiation and leak sites, BleepingComputer reports.
DataBreaches reports that AlphV claimed a breach at Viking Therapeutics and said an employee had filed an SEC complaint about it. The breach is unconfirmed.

In February 2024 unnamed sources told BleepingComputer the Change Healthcare attack was linked to BlackCat. BleepingComputer could not confirm this, and the gang had not claimed the attack at publication.

In March 2024 BleepingComputer reported that the gang appeared to be running an exit scam. Its leak and negotiation sites went offline and affiliates said they were unpaid. The gang offered its source code for $5 million and posted a fake FBI seizure banner. Europol and the NCA said they were not involved.
A US Justice Department release listed by Malpedia, dated 30 December 2025, says two Americans pleaded guilty to targeting US victims with ALPHV BlackCat ransomware.
Treat a gang's leak-site claim as unverified until the victim or investigators confirm it.
Review what access outside vendors hold on your network, and keep backups out of reach of ordinary admin accounts.
